stem: A 42-year-old patient with a long-standing history of psoriasis presents with joint pain and morning stiffness in the fingers and knees. You suspect psoriatic arthritis. Which investigation would be most appropriate initially to assess the extent of joint involvement?
stemHtml: Q 11: A 42-year-old patient with a long-standing history of psoriasis presents with joint pain and morning stiffness in the fingers and knees. You suspect psoriatic arthritis. Which investigation would be most appropriate initially to assess the extent of joint involvement? (Question Id: 515027)
keywords: Psoriasis – Indicates underlying systemic disease associated with arthritis; points toward psoriatic arthritis rather than other autoimmune arthropathies.
Joint pain and morning stiffness – Highlights musculoskeletal involvement, suggesting the need for joint imaging rather than skin or blood tests.
These keywords signal that the question is about assessing the extent of joint involvement in a patient with psoriasis, making X-ray of joints the most appropriate initial investigation.
keywordsHtml:
1. Psoriasis – Indicates underlying systemic disease associated with arthritis; points toward psoriatic arthritis rather than other autoimmune arthropathies.
  2. Joint pain and morning stiffness – Highlights musculoskeletal involvement, suggesting the need for joint imaging rather than skin or blood tests.
These keywords signal that the question is about assessing the extent of joint involvement in a patient with psoriasis, making X-ray of joints the most appropriate initial investigation.

D.title: X-ray of joints
D.body:
X-rays detect joint space narrowing, erosions, and new bone formation, which are characteristic in psoriatic arthritis.
Helps assess extent and pattern of joint involvement (distal interphalangeal joints, asymmetric involvement).
Extra note: Other imaging like MRI or ultrasound can detect early changes, but X-ray is the initial, practical investigation.
D.bodyHtml:
• X-rays detect joint space narrowing, erosions, and new bone formation, which are characteristic in psoriatic arthritis.
  • Helps assess extent and pattern of joint involvement (distal interphalangeal joints, asymmetric involvement).
  • Extra note: Other imaging like MRI or ultrasound can detect early changes, but X-ray is the initial, practical investigation.

A.title: ANA (Antinuclear Antibody)
A.body:
Used primarily to screen for autoimmune connective tissue diseases such as SLE.
Not specific or useful for assessing joint involvement in psoriatic arthritis.
A.bodyHtml:
• Used primarily to screen for autoimmune connective tissue diseases such as SLE.
  • Not specific or useful for assessing joint involvement in psoriatic arthritis.

B.title: RF (Rheumatoid Factor)
B.body:
Helps differentiate rheumatoid arthritis from seronegative arthropathies.
Most patients with psoriatic arthritis are RF-negative, so this is supportive but not for assessing joint damage.
B.bodyHtml:
• Helps differentiate rheumatoid arthritis from seronegative arthropathies.
  • Most patients with psoriatic arthritis are RF-negative, so this is supportive but not for assessing joint damage.

C.title: Skin biopsy
C.body:
Confirms psoriasis histologically but does not assess joint involvement.
Useful only if diagnosis of skin disease is unclear.
C.bodyHtml:
• Confirms psoriasis histologically but does not assess joint involvement.
  • Useful only if diagnosis of skin disease is unclear.

E.title: ESR alone
E.body:
ESR indicates inflammation but is non-specific.
Cannot define joint damage or involvement, only supportive for disease activity.
E.bodyHtml:
• ESR indicates inflammation but is non-specific.
  • Cannot define joint damage or involvement, only supportive for disease activity.

keyConcept:
Psoriatic arthritis is a seronegative inflammatory arthritis associated with psoriasis.
Initial assessment of joint involvement is best done with X-ray, as it shows characteristic erosions, joint space narrowing, and bony proliferation.
Blood tests (RF, ANA, ESR) or skin biopsy are supportive, but not primary for assessing joints.
keyConceptHtml:
• Psoriatic arthritis is a seronegative inflammatory arthritis associated with psoriasis.
  • Initial assessment of joint involvement is best done with X-ray, as it shows characteristic erosions, joint space narrowing, and bony proliferation.
  • Blood tests (RF, ANA, ESR) or skin biopsy are supportive, but not primary for assessing joints.

diagram.name: Psoriatic Arthritis – Initial Investigation of Joint Involvement
diagram.caption: This diagram highlights the initial diagnostic approach to joint involvement in psoriatic arthritis, emphasizing X-ray of joints as the first-line investigation. It illustrates characteristic radiographic findings such as joint space narrowing, erosions, and new bone formation, while showing that tests like RF, ANA, ESR/CRP, and skin biopsy are supportive or exclusionary but not primary for assessing joint damage.
